# `node:vm` against Node.js 25's own tests

Corpus: `nodejs/node@v25.0.0` `test/parallel/test-vm-*` — 92 files, listed in
[`NODE_TESTS.txt`](NODE_TESTS.txt). The per-test run is
[`RESULTS.md`](RESULTS.md) — currently **15 / 92**, of which 13 are real: the
two `test-vm-module-linkmodulerequests-*` files exit 0 on an unhandled
promise rejection ([zun#89](https://github.com/UrubuCode/zun/issues/89)) and
are nominal, which the table below records — regenerated by

```sh
bash tools/run_node_tests.sh --zun <path/to/zun> --module vm
```

The module is [`src/vm/vm.ts`](../../src/vm/vm.ts), pure Zun TypeScript over the
engine's own run-time compile path. Its tracker kind is `zun-ts` and it must be
run **without** `--ext`: `zun run --ext <lib> file.ts` goes through
`zun_vm::execute_with_extensions`, which injects no `EvalHost`, so
`new Function` — the floor this whole module stands on — answers
"code generation from strings disallowed" there while plain `zun run file.ts`
compiles and runs it. That is engine finding 3 below.

## Does this platform have run-time compilation?

It does, and the module is built on it rather than on an imitation of it.

| facility | present? | where |
|---|---|---|
| `new Function(p1, …, body)` / `Function(…)` | **yes** | lowered to the `functionConstruct` intrinsic (`zun_sema/src/check/builtins/object.rs`), answered by an injected `EvalHost` (`zun_interp/src/eval.rs`), implemented by the driver with the project's own compiler (`zun_vm/src/eval_host.rs` → `zun_compiler::compile_without_prelude`) |
| `eval` / indirect `eval` | **no** | not a realm binding and not declared by any prelude; `new Function` is the whole surface |
| a host/ABI entry that compiles source | **no** | `zun_abi` publishes natives *to* the engine; nothing goes the other way, so an extension cannot reach the compiler |
| ES module compilation / linking | **no** | `Module::link` (`zun_module/src/link.rs`) rejects any dynamically compiled module that declares or references a type, and there is no module-instantiation entry at all |
| a code cache | **no** | nothing serialises a compiled method range back out, so `cachedData` cannot be produced |
| interruptible execution | **no** | no way to unwind a running Tier-0 frame from outside, so `timeout`/`breakOnSigint` have nothing to act on |

What `new Function` *can* compile was probed one feature at a time: statements,
`let`/`const`/`var`, loops, `try`/`catch`/`finally`, arrow functions, nested
`function` declarations, object and array literals, `Math`, `Object`, `String`,
`Number`, `Map`, `Set`, `typeof`, string concatenation — all work. What it
cannot is in the next section.

## How a script and a context are expressed

Two gaps stand between `new Function(body)` and `vm.Script`, and the module
closes both with the compiler itself as the authority rather than with a guess.

**A completion value.** `new Function(body)` answers `undefined` unless `body`
returns; a Node `Script` answers the value of its last statement
(`vm.runInThisContext("'passed';")` is `'passed'`). `__vmScan` finds the
top-level statement boundaries — tracking line and block comments, the three
string forms, regular-expression literals and bracket depth — and `__vmCompile`
walks them from the last backwards, asking the real compiler whether
`<prefix> __zunVmR = (<suffix>);` compiles. The first split it accepts is the
one used. A boundary is only a *proposal*: a bad one fails to compile and is
discarded, and if none compiles the body runs as statements with the result
`undefined`, which is also the right answer for a script whose last statement
is not an expression.

**Contextified globals.** A free identifier *read* inside compiled code lowers
to `globalGet(name)`, so a name is visible if it is on the realm global; a free
identifier *write* is a **compile error** — ``unknown variable `foo` `` —
because the checker only lets an assignment reach `globalSet` for a name in the
compilation unit's own `module_globals` (`zun_sema/src/check/expr/assign.rs`),
and a dynamically compiled unit has none. That error is the mechanism: the
diagnostic *names* every implicitly assigned global (and names them all at once,
joined with `; `), so `__vmCompile` reads the names out of the message, declares
them as `let` at the top of the generated body initialised from the active
context, and copies them back in a `finally`. Reads are served by installing the
context object's own properties on the realm global for the run and restoring
them afterwards. Top-level `var` and `function` declarations are copied back
too, because in Node they become properties of the context global while `let`
and `const` do not — which is what `test-vm-function-declaration.js` pins.

So the generated program for `vm.runInContext('foo = 1; bar = 2; typeof baz;', ctx)`
is, literally:

```js
let foo = __zunVmCtx["foo"];
let bar = __zunVmCtx["bar"];
let __zunVmR;
try {
foo = 1; bar = 2;
__zunVmR = (typeof baz
);
} finally {
__zunVmCtx["foo"] = foo;
__zunVmCtx["bar"] = bar;
}
return __zunVmR;
```

**What this cannot be is a second realm.** The engine has one realm global, so a
context cannot *hide* the host's globals: `vm.runInNewContext('typeof process')`
answers `"object"` where Node answers `"undefined"`, and a script in a "new"
context can still reach every name the program declared. `createContext` marks
its object so `isContext` is exact, and the property bridge is exact for the
names a script reads and writes; isolation is the part that is missing, and the
table below says so for every file it costs.

## What is implemented

The whole documented surface, so that a blocker below is a blocker in the
engine rather than a gap in the module:

- `vm.Script` — `runInThisContext`, `runInContext`, `runInNewContext`,
  `createCachedData`, `sourceMapURL` (V8's `//# sourceMappingURL=` /
  `//@ ` magic comment, last occurrence wins), `cachedData`,
  `cachedDataProduced`, `cachedDataRejected`, `filename`, `lineOffset`,
  `columnOffset`. The source is compiled **in the constructor**, as V8 does, so
  a syntax error surfaces there and carries the compiler's own message.
- `vm.createContext` (including `vm.constants.DONT_CONTEXTIFY`), `vm.isContext`,
  `vm.createScript`, `vm.runInContext`, `vm.runInNewContext`,
  `vm.runInThisContext`, `vm.compileFunction`, `vm.measureMemory`,
  `vm.constants`.
- Every validator Node runs, in Node's order and with Node's messages:
  `options`/`options.filename`/`lineOffset`/`columnOffset`/`cachedData`/
  `produceCachedData`/`timeout`/`displayErrors`/`breakOnSigint`,
  `options.name`/`origin`/`codeGeneration.strings`/`codeGeneration.wasm`/
  `microtaskMode`, the `contextName`/`contextOrigin`/`contextCodeGeneration`
  renames, `params` as a string array, `parsingContext` as a `Context`,
  `contextExtensions` as an array of nullable objects, and
  `measureMemory`'s `mode`/`execution` one-of pairs.
- `compileFunction`'s parameters and `contextExtensions`, both of which work:
  `vm.compileFunction('return p + q + r + s + t', ['p','q','r','s','t'])('ab','cd','ef','gh','ij')`
  is `'abcdefghij'`, and
  `vm.compileFunction('return a;', undefined, { contextExtensions: [{ a: 5 }] })()`
  is `5`.

Two deliberate honest answers rather than fabrications:

- **no code cache.** `produceCachedData: true` sets `cachedDataProduced` to
  `false` and leaves `cachedData` absent; a supplied `cachedData` sets
  `cachedDataRejected` to `true`; `script.createCachedData()` throws
  `ERR_VM_CODE_CACHE_UNAVAILABLE` with its reason. An empty buffer accepted as
  valid cache would be a wrong answer, not an empty one.
- **`vm.Module` / `vm.SourceTextModule` / `vm.SyntheticModule` are absent**,
  which is precisely their shape in a Node run without
  `--experimental-vm-modules`. The bundler passes no V8 flags, and ES module
  instantiation needs a compile entry point this engine does not expose.
- `timeout` and `breakOnSigint` are validated and then ignored, because
  nothing can interrupt a running frame. A runaway script runs to completion.
- **`measureMemory` reports the one heap fact the host exposes.**
  `process.memoryUsage().heapUsed` is the `jsMemoryEstimate`, and
  `jsMemoryRange` is that single point rather than a fabricated interval; the
  option validation, the `summary`/`detailed` shapes and the
  `ExperimentalWarning` are Node's.

## New engine findings

All three were reduced to a standalone repro that needs nothing but the engine
binary, and all three were checked against the open **and** closed issue list
before being written down.

### 1. `new Error(...)` in dynamically compiled code evaluates to a function value

```ts
const f: any = new Function("return typeof new Error('m')");
console.log(f());                                   // zun: "function"   node: "object"
const g: any = new Function("throw new Error('boom')");
try { g(); } catch (e: any) { console.log(String(e), e.name, e.message); }
// zun: "[any] undefined undefined"       node: "Error: boom Error boom"
```

`Error` is a builtin class, and `Module::link`
(`crates/zun_module/src/link.rs:55`) forbids the type reference that
`new Error(...)` would need from a dynamically compiled module — so the
identifier resolves through `globalGet` to the realm *class descriptor* and
`new` on that descriptor yields the descriptor itself, **with no diagnostic**.
The value is opaque to the host: `typeof` says `"function"`,
`.name`/`.message` read back `undefined`, `instanceof Error` is `false`,
`String(e)` is `"[any]"`, and `Object.keys(e)` fails with "call did not resolve
to a method". `Date` is lost the same way (`typeof new Date()` is `undefined`)
and so are `Symbol`'s methods ("type Symbol has no methods") and `JSON`
("stringify is not a function") — all of them names that the eval host's
`zun_compiler::compile_without_prelude` (`crates/zun_vm/src/eval_host.rs:38`)
leaves without their definitions. Either the reference should be rejected with a
diagnostic or, better, dynamically compiled code should be able to link against
the host's builtin types. **Cost here: every file in the corpus that checks an
error thrown by a script** — `test-vm-static-this.js`,
`test-vm-new-script-this-context.js`, `test-vm-new-script-new-context.js`,
`test-vm-run-in-new-context.js` and the error half of several more.

### 2. `this.x = v` in dynamically compiled code panics the interpreter

```ts
const f: any = new Function("this.x = 'prop'; return 1");
f();
// thread '<unnamed>' panicked at crates\zun_interp\src\value.rs:228:22:
// expected object, found Void
```

`this` inside a compiled body is `undefined` — there is no function-`this` model
([zun#25](https://github.com/UrubuCode/zun/issues/25)) — and a member *store* on
it reaches `Value::as_object` (`crates/zun_interp/src/value.rs:228`), which
panics instead of throwing a `TypeError`. A `delete this.x` is fine and
`typeof this` answers `"undefined"`, so it is the store alone. An abort is
strictly worse than a catchable error for a library: the process dies and no
`try`/`catch` can see it. **Cost here: about fifteen files**, because
`this.<name> = …` and `Object.defineProperty(this, …)` are how Node's corpus
writes to a context global.

### 3. `zun run --ext <lib> file.ts` injects no `EvalHost`

```sh
$ cat q.ts
const f: any = new Function("return 1 + 1");
console.log(f());
$ zun run q.ts
2
$ zun run --ext <any extension> q.ts
zun: runtime error: unhandled exception: Str("EvalError: code generation from strings disallowed")
```

`zun run file.ts` goes through `zun_vm::execute_with`
(`crates/zun_vm/src/lib.rs:186`), which injects `CompilerEvalHost`;
`zun run --ext … file.ts` goes through
`zun_vm::execute_with_extensions_to_stdout` → `execute_with_extensions`
(`crates/zun_vm/src/lib.rs:253`), which calls `run_with(&module, output,
Some(&hook))` and passes no host at all. So loading *any* native extension
silently removes run-time code generation from the program, although the same
binary and the same `codegen` capability are in play. It is why this module's
tracker kind has to be `zun-ts` and why the CI entry excludes it from `--ext`.

### Already-known gaps that this module leans on

- `EvalHost::compile_function` types every parameter `number`
  (`crates/zun_vm/src/eval_host.rs:30`, marked "v1 typing"), so
  `new Function("s", "return s.length")` fails to compile with "type Float(F64)
  has no fields". `compileFunction` therefore does not use `new Function`
  parameters at all; it reads its arguments out of a realm-global array.
- a function value stored in a **class instance field** reads back `undefined`
  ([zun#17](https://github.com/UrubuCode/zun/issues/17) /
  [zun#19](https://github.com/UrubuCode/zun/issues/19)), so a compiled script's
  callable lives in a module-level map keyed by a number the `Script` carries.
- a closure returned through a **dynamic member call** reads as a non-callable
  box (same pair), which is why `compileFunction` is a canonical binding of
  `vm` in the bundler: `vm.compileFunction(...)` is rewritten to a static call.
- a closure that captures several bindings and is reached through a dynamic
  member call makes the engine throw "spread: value is not iterable" *before*
  the method body starts; `compileFunction`'s returned closure captures one
  number for that reason.
- a module-level `let` read inside a function answers an `Any`, and storing an
  `Any` in a binding declared `number` panics ("expected float, found Any"), so
  every mutable counter in `vm.ts` is declared `any` — the same shape the
  `punycode` work recorded.
- `arguments` is not available in a compiled body ("spread: value is not
  iterable").
